chapter: Howard McGhee's band and bebop in LA
title: Parker and Gillespie at Billy Berg's; the Casablanca
summary: Gillespie and Parker's band at Berg's, hanging out at the Casablanca, and Frank Morgan's arrival.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Charlie Parker: encounters, lore and legacy

blocks.x: In the meantime, this is just about the time when Dizzy Gillespie and Charlie Parker came to work for Billy Berg's with their fine group. They had Al Haig on piano, Stan Levey playing the drums, Ray Brown on bass, and Milt Jackson playing the vibes -- and later on, they added Lucky Thompson. So we hooked up again. Charlie Parker and the band, they were living at the Downtown House and I was still living at the Civic -- we were less than a half-a-block apart, you know. So we would manage to get together in the after-hour spots; we would all be hanging out in the after-hour places and everything. And it was really moving in Los Angeles at that time..

Oh yeah. The Casablanca was going good. Stanley Morgan eventually the owner of the Casablanca, the guitar player that had left us -- he eventually became the owner. And before too long, he had brought his son out here
from Milwaukee, Frank Morgan, was just getting himself together on his alto saxophone. He was sixteen, but he was a real good sixteen-year-old player, you know...

I think he was sixteen. Now, I think he was sixteen... But anyway, he was very young, and that's when he first came out. And Stanley brought him around to meet everybody. And we'd hang out in Stanley's place lots of nights, you know, because he had a small, intimate kind of place. And this is where I heard some classic works.
